page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal references: a note in the left margin beside the paragraph beginning "Iac.2.26." Running head at top, page number 120.

main_text.p: cata noftra, & emundet nos ab omni iniquita-te.
1. Ioan.2. 1. Si quis peccaverit, advocatum habemus apud Patrem, Iefum Chriftum juftum: & ipfe eft propitiatio pro peccatis noftris: non pro noftris autem tantum, fed etiam pro totius mundi.

p.i: 2. Qui Deum vere cognofcunt in ipfum credentes, eos fanctificationi & bonis operibus ftudere.

main_text.p: Iac.2. 26. Sicut corpus fine fpiritu mortuum eft: ita & fides fine operibus mortua eft. vid. etiam Gal.5.14 1.Ioan.2.3. In hoc fcimus, quod cognovimus eum (Deum & Chriftum) fi mandata ejus obfervemus. Qui dicit fe noffe eum, & mandata ejus non cuftodit, mendax eft, & in hoc veritas non eft.

Idemfic demonftratur. I. Quisquis ex Deo natus eft, is fanctitati, & bonis operibus ftudet. 1. Ioan.3. 10. In hoc manifefti funt filii Dei, & filii diaboli. Omnis, qui non eft juftus, non eft ex Deo, & qui non diligit fratrem fuum.
Omnis autem, qui credit, quoniam Iefus eft Chriftus, ex Deo natus eft, 1.Ioan.5. 1.
Ergo quifquis credit Iefum effe Chriftum, is fanctitati & bonis operibus ftudet.
II. Quisquis vitam aeternam habebit, is fanctificatus eft; ut patet ex Apoftoli dicto, Hebr. 12.14. Sine fanctimonia nemo videbit Deum.

p.i: Sed quisquis credit, is vitam aeternam habebit

page.notes: The left margin note "vid. etiam Gal.5.14" was placed beside the paragraph of "Iac.2.26." as printed. The reference "Ioan.3." at the end is printed right-aligned below the last line. The running head is given without the printed "Cap. 6." Some words in the scan are faint; the Greek-free text was read with care and no words are marked as uncertain.
